prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals and commitments (2001)

Health and care
- Recruit 27,500 nurses/midwives, 4,600 doctors, and 10,250 allied health professionals; add 10,000 hospital beds.
- Retention via average £1,000 annual pay rise for lowest‑paid NHS staff; review pay structures.
- Free personal care for long-term needs; restore free dental and eye checks; invest in scanners and diagnostics; £500m for NHS dentistry access.
- Pharmaceutical Agency to end regional “postcode” access differences and reduce drug costs; aim to reduce and ultimately scrap prescription charges.
- Patient Care Guarantees; stronger Health Ombudsman and Commons scrutiny; no‑fault compensation; independent advocacy; end mixed wards; ban age discrimination in care.
- Cut central targets; guarantee booked dates after GP referral.
- Environmental health: home energy audits, fuel‑poverty action, expanded air‑quality monitoring.

Education, skills and work
- Funded by +1p on basic income tax: average primary class sizes capped at 25; 5,000 extra secondary teachers; 40,000 more classroom assistants (25,000 in Key Stage 1); paid preparation time for primary teachers; training salaries for trainees; scrap performance‑related pay and SATs at age 7.
- Replace National Curriculum with a Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; individual learning plans; reform Ofsted; reduce bureaucracy.
- Early years: 1,000 specialists; nursery training and outdoor facilities.
- Abolish university tuition fees UK‑wide; restore grants for the poorest; raise loan repayment threshold to £13,000; improve academic pay equity.
- Lifelong learning entitlements up to Level 2 for all adults (Level 3 for 16–24s); simplify funding/qualifications; employer training incentives and reporting; paid study leave for 16–24s; regional targeting of employment funds.

Law, policing and justice
- 6,000 more police; 2,000 part‑time retained community officers; Community Safety Force for low‑level disorder; independent police complaints body.
- Prisons: expand work, skills and rehabilitation; greater use of effective community sentences; strengthen inspectorate; improve resettlement.
- Victims’ rights to be heard; tackle hate crime; retain jury trials in mid‑level cases; end most mandatory sentences; youth justice focused on rehabilitation; independent Department of Justice review and legal aid reform.
- National Crime Reduction Agency; independent Royal Commission on drugs.

Transport
- Free off‑peak local bus travel for pensioners and disabled people; aim half‑price for under‑19s in full‑time education.
- Emissions‑based Vehicle Excise Duty, abolishing it for the cleanest vehicles; no real‑terms rise in fuel tax per litre in the next Parliament.
- Expand local powers for congestion charging, parking levies, and bond finance for public transport.
- Sustainable Transport Authority overseeing rail, bus and more; stronger public control of rail investment; restructure Railtrack toward a not‑for‑profit public‑interest model; London Underground modernised via not‑for‑profit bonds.
- Rural transport fund; double rail freight by 2010; road safety target: −40% KSI by 2010; NATS kept not‑for‑profit.

Pensions, incomes and welfare
- Increase basic state pension, with larger rises for over‑75s and over‑80s; independent Pensions Authority for uprating advice; relax annuity rules; long‑term: universal basic pension entitlement and owned second pensions.
- Extend Winter Fuel Payments to the severely disabled.
- Minimum wage reviewed annually; same rate for ages 16+.
- Extra £200 per year for children in families on income support over a year; replace Child Support Agency with family courts; restore certain youth and housing benefits; simplify Housing Benefit; fairer utility tariffs.
- Long‑term tax aim: reduce 10p band to zero.

Culture, media and sport
- Arts at the core of schooling; restore free instrumental tuition; devolve arts funding; Local Initiatives Fund from Lottery receipts; libraries as free internet hubs.
- OFCOM as single communications regulator; redefine public service broadcasting; new BBC governance; additional 11pm watershed.
- Community Sports Plans; stronger school sport.

Business, consumers, energy and environment
- Cut red tape (sunset clauses, consultation); £1,500 small‑business rates allowance; promote mutuals and employee ownership.
- Increase public R&D (prioritise clean tech); Academy of British Invention; end use of export credits for arms to fund science.
- Replace Climate Change Levy with a carbon tax; emissions trading; 10% renewable electricity by 2010, rising 1% yearly; phase out nuclear at end of life; BNFL in public ownership.
- Stronger competition law against monopolies/local dominance; tighter bank rules (no anti‑competitive ATM fees, merger scrutiny); Post Office universal service; stronger consumer protection.
- Employee protections: tougher H&S enforcement; end compulsory retirement ages; extend consultation rights.

Constitution, governance and localism
- Referendum on AV+ for Westminster; STV for local and European elections; votes and candidacy at 16; expand postal/online voting.
- Replace House of Lords with elected Senate; create Supreme Court; stronger Commons committees and budget scrutiny; Civil Service Act.
- Devolution: more powers for Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland; elected English regional assemblies by referendum; needs‑based Finance Commission; replace Council Tax with local income tax.
- Strengthen Freedom of Information; citizens’ juries and initiatives; reduce number of ministers.

Civil liberties, immigration and asylum
- Equality Act covering discrimination across protected characteristics; Equality and Human Rights bodies; civil partnership registration.
- Judicial warrants for surveillance/interception; oppose ID cards; parliamentary oversight of security services.
- Asylum: faster, fairer decisions; replace vouchers with cash benefits; review dispersal; allow voluntary work and earlier paid work; fund local impacts; non‑discriminatory immigration policy aligned to skills needs.

Rural, housing, planning and environment
- National Recycling Programme (doorstep collections; 60% household recycling in 10 years); landfill tax escalator; flood defence taskforce.
- GM crop commercial moratorium to 2004 pending evidence.
- Fisheries: regional co‑management; extend inshore protections; modernise enforcement; Marine Protected Areas.
- CAP reform toward environmental/public goods; single Countryside Management Contracts; support tenant farmers and organic transition; create Ministry for Rural Affairs and Agricultural Ombudsman.
- Brownfield first via tax/planning reform; protect green spaces with new designations; require local permission for mobile masts; tackle homelessness; expand affordable and accessible housing; end 50% council tax rebate on second homes.

Europe
- Support enlargement; EU constitutional settlement defining competences and subsidiarity; greater transparency and accountability (Commission, Council, ECB minutes).
- Strengthen Westminster scrutiny of EU affairs; end European Parliament’s Strasbourg sessions.
- Common Foreign and Security Policy consistent with NATO.
- Enable euro entry at a sustainable rate subject to referendum; stop UK “gold‑plating” of EU rules; integrate environmental goals in EU policy.

Foreign policy, security and defence
- End subsidies for arms exports; parliamentary oversight of arms licensing; broker register and code.
- Prioritise conflict prevention; strengthen UN capacity, compliance auditing, peacekeeper training college in the UK, and rapid reaction for disasters.
- Support ICC; enhance Commonwealth role in governance and conflict resolution; maintain BBC World Service and British Council funding.
- Defence: maintain spending; prioritise mobility and joint operations; equal opportunity and family welfare in forces; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; oppose US National Missile Defense; moratorium on depleted uranium shells; day after Remembrance Sunday as public holiday.

Economy and tax
- Strengthen Bank of England independence (non‑renewable MPC terms, open appointments).
- Green Budget assessment; Green Tax Commission to shift tax from labour to pollution with revenue neutrality.
- Fund education via +1p basic rate; pensions/NHS via 50% rate over £100k and CGT reforms; police/transport via further CGT changes.
- Citizen’s Tax Contract to every household; pre‑Budget Fiscal Assessment by the MPC.
- Allow devolved governments, regions and councils to borrow for investment under fiscal rules.
- Euro referendum on entry at a competitive, sustainable rate.
